newsitem.title: USA: Hong Kong Cenbank sees no forex speculation on HK$.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong Cenbank sees no forex speculation on HK$.

text.p: The upcoming handover of Hong Kong to China is unlikely to result in foreign exchange speculations on the Hong Kong dollar, a senior Hong Kong Monetary Authority official said on Tuesday.
"There is no sign of speculatory pressure on the Hong Kong dollar and we have large foreign currency reserves," David Carse, deputy chief executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, told Reuters.
Carse spoke at a conference of the Bankers' Association for Foreign Trade where he presented a paper on global regulation.

Britain is set to handover sovereignty over Hong Kong to China on June 30, 1997. Under the notion of "one country, two systems," Hong Kong will operate as a Special Administrative region of China, retain its currency and central bank, and remain an international marketplace with free capital flows.
"Unlike other central banks, the mandate of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is not domestic price stability but to maintain the stability of the Hong Kong dollar versus the U.S. dollar," Carse said.
Carse said Hong Kong holds (U.S.) $63 billion in foreign exchange reserves and the People's Bank of China $100 billion.

"The primary responsibility for preserving the value of the Hong Kong dollar will reside with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, but the People's Bank of China is prepared to help out if needed," Carse pointed out, while adding there would be ample reserves to fend off speculative pressures if they were to arise.

"The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has the legal powers, monetary instruments and financial resources to fulfill its role as a central bank and maintain the value of the Hong Kong dollar," Carse also said. But he stressed financial markets have already displayed their confidence in a smooth handover.
